chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who enters the month of Ramadan while he is resident and does not intend to travel, then it occurs to him after entering Ramadan that he should travel. So he remained silent, and I asked him again. So he said: 'Residing is superior, unless he has a need that makes it inevitable for him to go out in it, or he fears for his wealth.'

key_terms.يَبْدُو لَهُ: It occurs to him / It becomes apparent to him

ai.seo_question: Is it better to stay home or travel during Ramadan if one initially planned to stay?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that for a resident (muqim) who initially intended to stay but later considers traveling during Ramadan, remaining in residence is the superior ruling (afdal). This preference holds unless there is a pressing necessity (hajah) or fear for one's wealth, highlighting the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving the full spiritual benefit of Ramadan prayers and fasting for those not on a journey.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from hs father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who enters into a Month of Ramazan and he is staying, not intending going out. Then he changes his mind after the entry of a Month of Ramazan that he should travel’. So he<sup>asws</sup> remained silent, and I asked him<sup>asws</sup> another time. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Staying is superior except if there happens to be for him a need which makes it inevitable for him for the going out in it, or he is fearing upon his wealth’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who when the month of Ramadan arrives is at home and does not want to travel; then it occurs to him, when it is the month of Ramadan, to travel. He (the Imam) remained quiet and I asked several times then he (the Imam) said, ‘Staying home is better unless he has a certain need for which it is necessary for him to travel or is afraid for his assets.’”
